Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

snap verb

break suddenly, with a crack

also snapped, snap in two, snap off, give way (of a branch, a rope)

classical

Ov. Ars 2.180: frangis, sī vīrēs experiēre tuās
Cic. N.D. 2.125: ōva, frangit (Lewis & Short)

frangō, frangere, frēgī, frāctum

verb, third conjugation

break; in the passive, snap, break in two

The everyday word for break. Of a stick, a bone or a bow that snaps, use the passive: rāmus frangitur, baculum frāctum est.

Other words

  • dissiliō, dissilīre, dissiluī — fly apart, burst asunder

    verb, fourth conjugation · also used · classical · Verg. A. 12.740–741: of a sword blade at a blow (Lewis & Short); Plin. NH 36.135: silex ignī (Lewis & Short)

    (vōx plērumque poētica: Lucr., Verg., Ov.; in prose Plin.)

    Of a thing that splits and flies apart at a blow or in the heat; it also means leap apart, as two bodies after a collision (Lucr. 1.385).

  • rumpō, rumpere, rūpī, ruptum — break, burst; of a rope or a string, snap

    verb, third conjugation · also used · classical

    For what breaks by being pulled or swelling: a string, a rope, a bag (see burst).

Examples

  • Arcum intentiō frangit, animum remissiō.

    Strain snaps the bow, slackness the mind.Ps.-Publ. A 33

  • Cavē: rāmus frangētur!

    Careful: the branch will snap!composed

See also broken, burst, snap one’s fingers, flexible.
